cards.b: Salt + hydrogen (for metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series).
Red in acid, blue in alkali.
Red in acid, yellow in alkali.
Red pH 1–2, orange/yellow pH 3–6, green pH 7, blue pH 8–11, purple pH 12–14.
Base: oxide or hydroxide of a metal. Alkali: a base that is soluble in water.
Reaction between an acid and an alkali to produce a salt and water.
Acidic: non-metal oxides (CO₂, SO₂). Basic: metal oxides (CuO, CaO).
Reacts with both acids and bases to form a salt and water, e.g. Al₂O₃, ZnO.

cards.f: Making a soluble salt from an insoluble base or carbonate
cards.b: Add excess solid to warm acid, filter off excess, evaporate part of filtrate, crystallise, dry.
Precipitation: mix two solutions, filter, wash residue with distilled water, dry.

cards.f: Test for carbonate / gas test for CO₂
cards.b: Add dilute acid: effervescence; CO₂ turns limewater milky.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: white, cream, yellow precipitate.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous barium nitrate: white precipitate.

short.q: Describe how to prepare pure, dry crystals of copper(II) sulfate from copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid. [4]
short.model: Add excess CuO to warm acid, filter off excess, heat filtrate to concentrate, leave to crystallise, filter and dry crystals.
points: excess copper oxide added to warm acid

short.q: Describe how aqueous sodium hydroxide can distinguish between aqueous Zn²⁺ and Ca²⁺. [3]
short.model: Both give a white precipitate. In excess NaOH the Zn²⁺ precipitate dissolves to a colourless solution; the Ca²⁺ precipitate does not.

short.q: State the test and result for sulfate ions. [3]
short.model: Add dilute nitric acid, then aqueous barium nitrate; a white precipitate shows sulfate.

short.q: Write a word equation for sulfuric acid reacting with sodium hydroxide, and name the type of reaction. [2]
short.model: Sulfuric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium sulfate + water; neutralisation.

short.q: Classify SO₂ and CaO as acidic or basic oxides and explain how you can tell. [3]
short.model: SO₂ is acidic (non-metal oxide, reacts with bases); CaO is basic (metal oxide, reacts with acids).
